item.text: {"question_id":"7B.9","answer":"For the 2023 period, the evidence supports allegations of favoritism and privileged network access involving relatives and associates, but not a finding that López Obrador personally directed or benefited from particular contracts. Reports described contracts to friends of his son, including alleged simulated competition and more than 100 million pesos in government-linked work (BATCH-0008-E007; BATCH-0008-E011). Earlier cases involving Segalmex, the president’s friend Ignacio Ovalle, and alleged family-linked contracting provide relevant background entering 2023, while remaining allegations or investigations rather than final findings (BATCH-0046-E008; BATCH-0005-E004). Personal attribution is stronger for knowledge, public defense, and tolerance: López Obrador defended relatives and denied conflicts, while also ordering a review of the Baker Hughes matter and requesting transfer of his brother’s case file to the electoral authority (BATCH-0008-E011; BATCH-0042-E001). A reported pattern of protecting close collaborators and treating Segalmex as the only corruption case is an adverse analytical assessment, not proof of each underlying act or presidential direction (BATCH-0026-E003). Contrary evidence includes the closure of the Pío investigation, government corruption investigations and penalties, and recovery action against corruption attributed to a prior administration (BATCH-0005-E003; BATCH-0004-E015; BATCH-0012-E011). The defensible conclusion is a materially concerning but unresolved pattern of family-and-associate access and possible tolerance, with uncertain personal benefit, incomplete 2023-specific evidence, and no established direct instruction for individual procurement or enforcement
